diagrams.title: 8086 internal architecture
diagrams.cap: BIU fetches instructions into the queue while EU executes — this overlap (pipelining) speeds up the 8086.

formulas.name: 8086 basics
f: 16-bit processor, 16-bit data bus, 20-bit address bus → 1 MB

formulas.name: BIU and EU
f: BIU: segment registers, IP, address adder, 6-byte instruction
EU: ALU, general registers, flags, decoder
notes: Tip: The queue lets fetch and execute overlap (pipelining).

formulas.name: Registers
f: General : AX, BX, CX, DX (8 −bit halves AHAL …)
notes: Tip: CX = counter for loops/strings; BX = base; DX = I/O port / multiply high word.

formulas.name: Flags (9)
f: Status (6): CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, OF
notes: Tip: 8085 has 5 flags; 8086 adds OF and three control flags.

formulas.name: Addressing modes
notes: Tip: MOV AX, [BX+SI+04H] = based-indexed with displacement.

formulas.name: Instruction groups
f: Data transfer, arithmetic, logical, shift/rotate, string, branch
notes: Tip: REP prefix repeats string instructions CX times.

formulas.name: 8086 interrupts
f: type 0 divide error, 1 single-step, 2 NMI, 3 breakpoint, 4
notes: Tip: Each vector = 4 bytes (IP then CS).

formulas.name: Minimum / maximum mode
f: MN/MX pin: minimum (single processor, 8086 makes control
notes: Tip: Memory is split into even (A0 = 0) and odd (BHE = 0) banks.

formulas.name: 8255 PPI
f: Mode 0 simple I/O, Mode 1 strobed (handshake), Mode 2
BSR mode for single bits of port C
notes: Where: PPI = programmable peripheral interface; BSR = bit set/reset
Tip: Control word D7 = 1 → I/O mode; D7 = 0 → BSR mode.

formulas.name: 8253/8254 timer
f: 6 modes: 0 interrupt on terminal count, 1 one-shot, 2 rate
generator, 3 square wave, 4 software strobe, 5 hardware strobe
notes: Tip: Output frequency (mode 3) = input clock / count.

formulas.name: 8279 keyboard/display
f: Scans a 64-key matrix and drives 16-digit display
notes: Tip: Relieves the CPU from scanning and debouncing.

formulas.name: 8257 DMA controller
notes: Tip: DMA is the fastest data transfer method.

formulas.name: ARM & PIC basics
f: ARM: 32-bit RISC, load/store architecture, 16 visible registers
(R13 SP, R14 LR, R15 PC), CPSR, Thumb mode
PIC: Harvard architecture, RISC (≈ 35 instructions in
notes: Tip: Both are RISC; 8085/8086 are CISC.

why.cause: physical address = segment × 16 + offset → 20 bits → 1 MB
why.effect: Shift the segment left by one hex digit and add.

why.cause: BIU fetches while EU executes (6-byte queue) → pipelining
MN/MX pin → single or multiprocessor mode
why.effect: Max mode uses the 8288 bus controller.

why.cause: 8255 control word decides each port's mode and direction
why.effect: Mode 0 simple I/O, mode 1 handshake, mode 2 bidirectional.

st: 8086 basics
16-bit processor, 16-bit data bus, 20-bit address bus → 1 MB memory; clock 5–10 MHz
BIU and EU
BIU: segment registers, IP, address adder, 6-byte instruction queue (pipelining); EU: ALU, general registers, flags, decoder
Registers
General: AX, BX, CX, DX (8-bit halves AH/AL …); pointer/index: SP, BP, SI, DI; segment: CS, DS, SS, ES; IP; flag register
Flags (9)
Status (6): CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, OF; Control (3): TF (trap), IF (interrupt), DF (direction)
Addressing modes
Immediate, register, direct, register-indirect, based, indexed, based-indexed, relative-based-indexed, string, I/O (direct/indirect)
Instruction groups
Data transfer, arithmetic, logical, shift/rotate, string, branch (JMP, CALL, LOOP), processor control
8086 interrupts
256 types; IVT at 00000H–003FFH (1 KB); vector of type n at 4n; type 0 divide error, 1 single-step, 2 NMI, 3 breakpoint, 4 overflow
Minimum / maximum mode
MN/MX pin: minimum (single processor, 8086 makes control signals) vs maximum (multiprocessor, 8288 bus controller)
8255 PPI
3 ports (A, B, C = 24 I/O lines); Mode 0 simple I/O, Mode 1 strobed (handshake), Mode 2 bidirectional (port A only); BSR mode for single bits of port C
3 independent 16-bit down counters; 6 modes: 0 interrupt on terminal count, 1 one-shot, 2 rate generator, 3 square wave, 4 software strobe, 5 hardware strobe
8279 keyboard/display
Scans a 64-key matrix and drives 16-digit display; 8-byte FIFO for keys, 16-byte display RAM
8257 DMA controller
4 channels; transfers memory ↔ I/O without CPU using HOLD/HLDA; 14-bit count → 16 KB per block
ARM & PIC basics
ARM: 32-bit RISC, load/store architecture, 16 visible registers (R13 SP, R14 LR, R15 PC), CPSR, Thumb mode; PIC: Harvard architecture, RISC (≈ 35 instructions in mid-range), on-chip peripherals
